page: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a dedicated CPU virtual server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical AMD EPYC cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 188.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled locally, consisting of a 960 GB NVMe SSD, while no dedicated GPU hardware is present. The hypervisor layer is managed via QEMU.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng scores placing the instance in the top 25% of tested hardware. The AMD EPYC processor demonstrates strong capabilities in cryptographic operations, database transactions, and software compilation, as evidenced by high Passmark CPU encryption and database operations scores. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is also highly efficient, ranking in the top 25%, though memory read bandwidth and overall Passmark memory scores remain in the average tier. For specialized workloads, the instance achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small language models, though performance scales down to average levels when processing medium and large models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ccx63 offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated CPU cores with a substantial memory allocation and fast local NVMe storage without the premium cost of GPU accelerators. This resource profile makes the instance highly suitable for multi-threaded applications, database hosting, software compilation pipelines, and lightweight machine learning inference. It is also well-suited for high-throughput web serving and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring predictable, dedicated compute resources.
